title_en: Police ban protests near 10 schools and five universities in Paris
title_zh: 巴黎警方禁止在 10 所学校和 5 所大学附近举行抗议活动
summary: The order will be in place from 16 to 20 November, Paris police chief Patrice Faure says.
summary_zh: 巴黎警察局长帕特里斯·福雷 (Patrice Faure) 表示，该命令将于 11 月 16 日至 20 日期间生效。
body_en: Police in Paris have issued a five-day ban on protests near 10 secondary schools and five universities as authorities try to control weeks of blockades and violence at educational venues in France.
The order prohibits unauthorised gatherings or marches within 100m of the sites from 16 to 20 November.

Paris police chief Patrice Faure said the ban was necessary due to "numerous disruptions and blockades around certain secondary schools and establishments of higher learning" and "persistent violence".
A wave of protests began in France September over poor secondary school conditions, before spreading to universities, workers and a "yellow-vest" movement against the cost of living.

Announcing the order, the Paris police chief said blockades around certain secondary schools and universities have led to damaged public property, violence against members of the educational community and clashes with law enforcement.
Mayors of eight Parisian districts had contacted the regional education authority to call for measures to "secure the entrances and exits" of blockaded secondary schools, local media report.
Some 1,548 people have been arrested in Paris since the start of the protests, Faure said on Sunday.
On Saturday, 106,000 people from a range of groups took to the streets in France, including 24,000 in Paris, the interior ministry said.
It marked the fifth Saturday in a row where students, unions and yellow-vest activists went out to protest.
The number of protesters was much lower than previously, and so was the number of those arrested, the ministry said - 219 across the country, including 45 in Paris.
body_zh: 巴黎警方对 10 所中学和 5 所大学附近的抗议活动发布了为期五天的禁令，当局试图控制法国教育场所持续数周的封锁和暴力事件。
该命令禁止 11 月 16 日至 20 日期间在该地点 100m 范围内进行未经授权的集会或游行。
巴黎警察局长帕特里斯·福尔表示，由于“某些中学和高等教育机构周围发生了许多干扰和封锁”以及“持续的暴力事件”，这项禁令是必要的。
9月，法国因中学条件恶劣而引发抗议浪潮，随后蔓延至大学、工人和反对生活成本的“黄背心”运动。
巴黎警察局长在宣布这一命令时表示，对某些中学和大学的封锁导致公共财产受损、针对教育界成员的暴力行为以及与执法部门的冲突。
据当地媒体报道，巴黎八个区的市长已联系地区教育当局，呼吁采取措施“确保被封锁中学的出入口安全”。
福尔周日表示，自抗议活动开始以来，巴黎已有约 1,548 人被捕。
内政部表示，周六，来自不同群体的 106,000 人走上法国街头，其中巴黎有 24,000 人。
这是学生、工会和黄背心活动人士连续第五个周六外出抗议。
该部表示，抗议者人数比之前少得多，被捕人数也少得多，全国有 219 人，其中巴黎有 45 人。

title_en: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urge Israel to allow aid into Gaza
title_zh: 澳大利亚、加拿大、意大利和英国敦促以色列允许援助进入加沙
summary: The countries accuse Israel of preventing tents and other supplies from entering Gaza, despite the humanitarian crisis.
summary_zh: 这些国家指责以色列不顾人道主义危机，阻止帐篷和其他物资进入加沙。
body_en: Share Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urge Israel to allow aid into Gaza on social media
Gaza floods leave 350,000 affected as UN humanitarian chief demands aid access

Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom have ⁠⁠⁠⁠urged Israel to allow immediate and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza, highlighting that recent floods have “brought further suffering” for Palestinians living there.
The countries’ foreign ministers co-signed Sunday’s joint statement , the latest international warning about the dire humanitarian situation in the besieged territory.

“People in Gaza desperately need shelter and humanitarian assistance,” the statement said. “Yet 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border and prevented from entering Gaza.”
For years, Israel has restricted entry and exports into Gaza, home to more than 2 million people.

But since the start of its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, Israel has placed the Palestinian territory under a full-scale blockade, limiting access to even essential supplies like food and water.
Under the Geneva Convention, denying civilians access to humanitarian aid can constitute a war crime.
“We today urge the Government of Israel to stop the delays now and allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza,” Sunday’s statement said.
Heavy rain this month swept away tens of thousands of tents in the territory, leaving many without shelter.
“This situation is entirely reversible”, Sunday’s statement said, “and there is still time to act before the winter fully sets in”.
More than 1.9 million people have been displaced in Gaza, according to the United Nations, many of them suffering displacement multiple times.

As of November 1, the Global Shelter Cluster, a humanitarian organisation that coordinates with the Red Cross and the UN, estimated that Gaza residents need at least 1.7 million mattresses and 121,000 tents to face this season’s cold, rainy weather.
During Israel’s genocidal war, entire neighbourhoods and cities were levelled. Some of the structures that remain are unstable.
In September, at least 20 people were killed when a building they were sheltering in collapsed.
Shelter is only one factor in the ongoing humanitarian crisis, though.

Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians in Gaza have been plunged into poverty since Israel began its genocidal war. The price of basic goods has soared as incomes have shrunk due to the war and Israel’s tightened siege.

两国外长周日共同签署了联合声明，这是国际社会对被围困地区严峻的人道主义局势发出的最新警告。

声明称：“加沙人民迫切需要庇护所和人道主义援助。” “然而，有 15 万顶帐篷和其他重要物资被扣留在边境，无法进入加沙。”
多年来，以色列一直限制进入和出口人口超过 200 万的加沙地带。
但自 2023 年 10 月对加沙发动种族灭绝战争以来，以色列对巴勒斯坦领土进行了全面封锁，甚至限制了食物和水等基本物资的获取。
根据《日内瓦公约》，拒绝平民获得人道主义援助可能构成战争罪。
周日的声明称：“我们今天敦促以色列政府立即停止拖延，并允许人道主义援助立即、迅速和不受阻碍地进入整个加沙。”
本月的大雨冲毁了境内数万顶帐篷，导致许多人无家可归。
周日的声明称，“这种情况是完全可逆转的，在冬季完全到来之前仍有时间采取行动”。
据联合国称，加沙已有超过 190 万人流离失所，其中许多人多次流离失所。
截至 11 月 1 日，与红十字会和联合国协调的人道主义组织全球避难所估计，加沙居民至少需要 170 万张床垫和 121,000 个帐篷来应对本季寒冷多雨的天气。
在以色列的种族灭绝战争期间，整个社区和城市都被夷为平地。一些保留下来的结构是不稳定的。
9 月，至少 20 人因避难建筑物倒塌而丧生。
不过，庇护所只是当前人道主义危机的因素之一。
自以色列开始种族灭绝战争以来，加沙地带的数十万巴勒斯坦人陷入贫困。由于战争和以色列加强围困，收入减少，基本商品的价格飙升。

title_en: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media
title_zh: 捷克人集会反对改变公共媒体资助计划
summary: Protesters say the move will stifle media freedom, while the government insists broadcasters need to cut costs.
summary_zh: 抗议者表示此举将扼杀媒体自由，而政府则坚称广播公司需要削减成本。
body_en: Thousands of people have gathered in central Prague to protest against the Czech government's plans to scrap the licence fee and use the state budget to fund public media.
Critics say the plans would allow politicians to stifle media freedom.

The coalition government - which consists of the populist ANO party and two right-wing Eurosceptic parties - insists the change will not affect editorial independence, but wants broadcasters to cut costs.
Parliament passed the first draft of the proposal late last month. Since then, thousands of Czechs have taken part in protests.
Czech households currently pay ⁠205 crowns ($9.44; £7.06) a month for public TV and radio.
Sunday's protest was organised by the Million Moments for Democracy association which said "roughly 400,000" people had attended.
"I know that our entire Czech Television is a guarantee of truth and objectivity," pensioner Milana Rudolfova, 72, told Reuters news agency.
"If we do not have public television and radio then unfortunately we will not be able to believe anything anymore."
Prime Minister Andrej Babis has insisted the government does not want to control public media.

"The funding system is changing, no one wants to control public media, no one wants to dictate to them what they should say and do, no one wants to nationalise them," Babis told the Czech News Agency.
"We are doing this because the system is already outdated and most of Europe is going the same way today and others are joining in," he added.
Some European countries, including France and Norway, have moved away from the public licence fee model in the last few years.
France removed it in 2022 and its public media, which also carries advertising, is now funded by a portion of the income from VAT.
Norway abolished its license fee in 2020 and moved its public broadcaster's funding into the national budget.
Reuters said the proposal would amount to a 15% cut in funding for the public broadcasters Czech TV and Czech Radio.
Some protesters wore pointed hats folded out of newspapers as a tribute to an animated character, Vecernicek, who has introduced Czech Television's nightly children's bedtime stories for decades.
Critics have compared the government's media bill to changes in Hungary under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who tightly controlled state media when he was in power.
Prime Minister Andrej Babis was appointed in December in 2025, and has faced criticism over his coalition's attacks on Czech media.

"Political attacks against private and public media have become one of the hallmarks of Andrej Babis' premiership," said Pavol Szalai, Prague Bureau director of international press freedom organisation Reporters Without Borders, in June.
Czech billionaire becomes PM with promise to cut ties to business empire
body_zh: 数千人聚集在布拉格市中心，抗议捷克政府取消许可费并使用国家预算资助公共媒体的计划。
批评者称，这些计划将允许政客扼杀媒体自由。
由民粹主义 ANO 党和两个右翼欧洲怀疑论党组成的联合政府坚称这一变化不会影响编辑独立性，但希望广播公司削减成本。
议会上个月末通过了该提案的初稿。此后，数千名捷克人参加了抗议活动。
捷克家庭目前每月为公共电视和广播支付 205 克朗（9.44 美元；7.06 英镑）。
周日的抗议活动是由“民主百万时刻”协会组织的，该协会称“大约有 40 万人”参加了抗议活动。
72 岁的养老金领取者米拉娜·鲁多尔芙娃 (Milana Rudolfova) 告诉路透社：“我知道我们整个捷克电视台都是真实性和客观性的保证。”
“如果我们没有公共电视和广播，那么不幸的是我们将无法再相信任何事情。”
总理安德烈·巴比斯坚称政府不想控制公共媒体。
巴比斯告诉捷克通讯社：“资助体系正在发生变化，没有人想控制公共媒体，没有人想向他们发号施令，他们应该说什么和做什么，没有人想将他们国有化。”
“我们这样做是因为这个系统已经过时了，欧洲大部分地区今天也在走同样的路，其他国家也正在加入，”他补充道。
包括法国和挪威在内的一些欧洲国家在过去几年中已经放弃了公共许可费模式。
法国于 2022 年取消了这一政策，其公共媒体（也有广告）现在由增值税收入的一部分提供资金。
挪威于 2020 年取消了牌照费，并将其公共广播公司的资金纳入国家预算。
路透社称，该提案将相当于公共广播公司捷克电视台和捷克广播电台的资金削减 15%。
一些抗议者戴着用报纸折叠起来的尖顶帽子，以向动画人物韦切尔尼切克致敬，几十年来，他一直介绍捷克电视台每晚的儿童睡前故事。
批评者将政府的媒体法案与匈牙利前总理欧尔班·维克多(Viktor Orbán)领导下发生的变化进行比较，后者在执政期间严格控制国家媒体。
总理安德烈·巴比斯 (Andrej Babis) 于 2025 年 12 月被任命，并因其联盟对捷克媒体的攻击而面临批评。
国际新闻自由组织无国界记者布拉格分社主任帕沃尔·萨莱 (Pavol Szalai) 6 月表示：“针对私人和公共媒体的政治攻击已成为安德烈·巴比斯 (Andrej Babis) 总理任期的标志之一。”

title_en: Thousands of US flights still cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide
title_zh: 全国飞机停飞两天后，数千架美国航班仍被取消或延误
summary: The US transport secretary says that normal air-traffic operations may not be restored until Monday.
summary_zh: 美国交通部长表示，正常的空中交通运营可能要到周一才能恢复。
body_en: Thousands of US flights cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide - BBC News
Thousands of US flights were cancelled or delayed on Sunday as the US air-traffic control system continued to recover from a technical failure that led to a rare national ground stop.
Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said normal operations may not be restored until Monday.
"We have airplanes and crews that are out of position, so it takes a little bit of time," he told the BBC's US partner CBS. More than 5,000 flights were delayed and 2,000 cancelled on Sunday.

President Donald Trump urged Congress on Sunday to approve more money to modernise the air-traffic control system. The grounding of all aircraft scheduled to depart the US on Friday caused chaos at airports across the country.

More than 3,500 airplanes were in the air when the FAA announced at 15:54 EST (20:54 GMT) that flights would be grounded until further notice. Some were diverted to other airports and others flew on to their destinations.
In the aftermath, 8,500 flights were delayed and another 8,000 cancelled, according to FlightAware.

The stoppage left passengers stuck inside planes on the tarmac, unable to take off or to return to their gates. Others were stranded in airports, sleeping on the floor and desperately trying to get in touch with their airline. The ground stop also had a knock-on effect on schedules around the world, with some flights out of the UK and Europe cancelled.
The ground stop was lifted after about four and a half hours, but the impacts continued over the weekend.
On Saturday, airlines cancelled more than 5,900 flights and more than 7,000 others were delayed.

Investigators are still working to determine the root cause and who is at fault, but Duffy said the administration decided to ground flights after failures in a key system that allows air traffic controllers and pilots to communicate.
The transport secretary said a computer router installed as part of an upgrade from copper wire to fibre started sending out faulty signals.
He said on Sunday that the router - a piece of equipment which directs traffic across the network - was installed in El Dorado, Arkansas, and "flooded our network".
Duffy said that issues will continue to arise until the US makes major modernising changes to its air control system. The system needs a complete overhaul, he said.
"Let's not lie to each other," he said on NBC's Meet The Press. "We have to make investments into a network that has been neglected for decades."
In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump urged US lawmakers to allocate the money, saying "we can get it built quickly and efficiently".

"It will be the BEST SYSTEM anywhere in the World. Much of our current air control system is 50 years old - RIDICULOUS! We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs," he said.
Experts say the US uses antiquated technology for flight communications.
Aviation analyst Miles O'Brien described the US system as "a house that's about to be condemned".
He told the BBC: "I think most of us could look at this and go 'this is a system in the United States that we have allowed to decay'. It is worse than a fixer-upper."
body_zh: 全国飞机停飞两天后，数千架美国航班被取消或延误 -_澳门赌博平台

交通部长肖恩·达菲表示，正常运营可能要到周一才能恢复。
他对 BBC 美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) 表示：“我们的飞机和机组人员都处于失位状态，因此需要一点时间。”周日有超过 5,000 架航班延误，2,000 架航班取消。
唐纳德·特朗普总统周日敦促国会批准更多资金来实现空中交通管制系统的现代化。所有计划于周五离开美国的飞机均停飞，导致全国机场出现混乱。
美国东部时间 15:54（格林尼治标准时间 20:54），美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 宣布航班将停飞，直至另行通知。当时，超过 3,500 架飞机正在空中飞行。一些飞机被转移到其他机场，另一些则飞往目的地。
据 FlightAware 称，此后有 8,500 架航班延误，另有 8,000 架航班取消。
这次停飞导致乘客被困在停机坪上的飞机内，无法起飞或返回登机口。其他人则被困在机场，睡在地板上，拼命试图与航空公司取得联系。这次地面停留还对世界各地的航班时刻表产生了连锁反应，一些从英国和欧洲起飞的航班被取消。
大约四个半小时后，地面停止被解除，但影响在周末仍在继续。
周六，航空公司取消了 5,900 多个航班，另有 7,000 多个航班延误。
调查人员仍在努力确定根本原因和责任方，但达菲表示，在允许空中交通管制员和飞行员进行通信的关键系统出现故障后，政府决定停飞航班。
交通部长表示，作为从铜线升级到光纤的一部分而安装的计算机路由器开始发出错误信号。
他周日表示，路由器——一种引导网络流量的设备——安装在阿肯色州埃尔多拉多，“淹没了我们的网络”。
达菲表示，在美国对其空中控制系统进行重大现代化改造之前，问题将继续出现。他说，该系统需要彻底检修。
“我们不要互相撒谎，”他在 NBC 的“与媒体会面”节目中说道。 “我们必须对几十年来被忽视的网络进行投资。”
特朗普周日在《Truth Social》上发表帖子，敦促美国立法者分配这笔资金，并表示“我们可以快速有效地建设它”。
“这将是世界上最好的系统。我们现有的空气控制系统大部分已有 50 年历史了——太荒谬了！我们已经开始了这项工作，但应该一次性完成，而不是一点一滴地完成，”他说。
专家表示，美国使用过时的飞行通信技术。
航空分析师迈尔斯·奥布莱恩将美国的系统描述为“一座即将受到谴责的房子”。
他告诉英国广播公司：“我认为我们大多数人都会看到这一点，然后说‘这是美国的一个系统，我们任由它腐烂’。它比修缮更糟糕。”

body_en: The Israeli military said on Sunday its forces had killed a senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza. The militant group confirmed the death of Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, adding that he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks.

title_en: Clothing factories shut in Bangladesh as workers strike over pay
title_zh: 孟加拉国服装厂因工人工资罢工而关闭
summary: Workers are striking over demands for a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) a month.
summary_zh: 工人们因要求每月 30,000 塔卡（182 英镑）的最低工资而举行罢工。
body_en: Dozens of factories in Bangladesh's main clothes-producing area have been shut by workers striking over a higher minimum wage.
Nearly 150 sites across the country have been closed in the textile hubs of Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur this weekend.
The garment industry is big business for Bangladesh, generating nearly $40bn (£30bn) in exports every year and making up 10% of the country's total GDP.

Workers are striking over demands for a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) a month. The minimum monthly wage in Bangladesh is currently 12,500 taka but employees say this is not enough to deal with the cost of living crisis.
On Sunday morning workers massed on the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur to block the road. Traffic was stopped by the protests for about an hour before police stepped in.
A "No Work No Pay" provision of labour laws allows owners to suspend operations and withhold wages when production is disrupted.
Police Supt Mohammad Amjad Hossain told the BBC officers shut factories in the city after the workers walked out.
He said 13 factories were closed on Saturday night and "sixteen factories were closed during the morning unrest".
Wage protests force hundreds of Bangladesh garment factories to close
The garment industry in Bangladesh employs about four million workers making clothes for big brands including H&M, Primark and Zara.

Bangladesh is the world's second largest exporter of ready- to-wear clothes after China and it is feared that the current unrest could have a knock-on effect for international buyers if it carries on for substantial amount of time.
The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) is calling for protection for factories.

"BGMEA and BKMEA have questioned the justification of continuing to participate in wage board negotiations without any assurance that the factories will be protected," BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan said.
"Garment factories that have been unable to continue production due to the ongoing unrest will remain indefinitely closed from tomorrow under... Bangladesh's labour law."
On 1 November the government formed a minimum wage board to recommend a revised pay structure for workers.
The board, chaired by a senior district judge, said at its first meeting it would finalise any recommendations by the end of November.
Once it is put in place, the revised pay structure is expected to take effect from 1 December.
body_zh: 孟加拉国主要服装产区的数十家工厂因工人因提高最低工资而罢工而关闭。
本周末，萨瓦尔、阿苏利亚和加济布尔等纺织中心的全国近 150 个工厂已关闭。
服装业是孟加拉国的大产业，每年产生近 400 亿美元（300 亿英镑）的出口额，占该国 GDP 总额的 10%。
工人们因要求每月 30,000 塔卡（182 英镑）的最低工资而举行罢工。目前孟加拉国的最低月工资为12,500塔卡，但员工表示这不足以应对生活成本危机。
周日早上，工人们聚集在加济布尔的达卡-坦盖尔高速公路上，封锁道路。抗议活动导致交通中断约一个小时，随后警察介入。
劳动法中的“无工作无报酬”条款允许业主在生产中断时暂停运营并扣发工资。
警察局长穆罕默德·阿姆贾德·侯赛因告诉英国广播公司，在工人罢工后，官员关闭了该市的工厂。
他说，周六晚上有 13 家工厂关闭，“早上骚乱期间有 16 家工厂关闭”。
工资抗议迫使数百家孟加拉国服装厂关闭
孟加拉国的服装业雇佣了约 400 万名工人，为 H&M、Primark 和 Zara 等大品牌生产服装。
孟加拉国是仅次于中国的全球第二大成衣出口国，人们担心当前的骚乱如果持续很长一段时间，可能会对国际买家产生连锁反应。
孟加拉国服装制造商和出口商协会（BGMEA）和孟加拉国针织品制造商和出口商协会（BKMEA）呼吁保护工厂。
BGMEA 主席马哈茂德·哈桑·汗 (Mahmud Hasan Khan) 表示：“BGMEA 和 BKMEA 对在不保证工厂受到保护的情况下继续参加工资委员会谈判的合理性提出质疑。”
“根据孟加拉国的劳动法，由于持续的骚乱而无法继续生产的服装工厂将从明天起无限期关闭。”
11 月 1 日，政府成立了最低工资委员会，建议修改工人的工资结构。
该委员会由一名高级地区法官担任主席，在第一次会议上表示，将在 11 月底之前敲定所有建议。
一旦实施，修订后的薪酬结构预计将于 12 月 1 日生效。

title_en: Judge blocks Trump closure of 'Trash Island' Washington DC golf course on Sunday
title_zh: 法官阻止特朗普周日关闭“垃圾岛”华盛顿特区高尔夫球场
summary: The temporary order is part of a months-long challenge to the US president's plans to upgrade East Potomac Golf Links into a championship course.
summary_zh: 这项临时命令是对美国总统将东波托马克高尔夫球场升级为锦标赛球场的计划长达数月挑战的一部分。
body_en: A federal judge has temporarily blocked the US government's closure of an historic golf course and park in Washington DC.
US District Judge Ana Reyes has been overseeing a months-long challenge to the president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links, which he said would be closed from 15 November for extensive renovations.
Reyes has said President Donald Trump cannot close the park nor its golf course, but added that his administration was not required to actively manage either.

Trump, an avid golfer, has said his plans to upgrade the 106-year-old course will create "one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World". The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

Declaring the current course "Trash Island", he announced in October that it would be renovated over 15 months to create a space that "will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments" - despite the ongoing litigation.

Reyes said in a 30-page decision issued on Saturday that the Trump administration's justifications for the proposed course closures were pretextual and that the government had violated at least two federal laws "to meet an arbitrary deadline".
"The government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely," Reyes wrote.

She said the closure "runs counter to the public interest in utilising national parkland", adding that the government had not "plausibly identified any harm it would suffer from a temporary restraining order that preserves the status quo pending further proceedings".
'Trash Island' or DC landmark? How a golf course got Trump in a messy legal dispute

A coalition of advocacy and legal groups opposing the closure and renovation said they are "grateful that the court has stopped the government from unlawfully closing East Potomac Park and depriving people of this priceless piece of American history and wonderful recreation space".

"Our laws prevent this administration from acting without a fair and public process, and today's order will stop the government from ignoring those laws," said the coalition, which represents the plaintiffs and includes Democracy Forward and the Democracy Defenders Fund. "We are eager to continue to argue this case in court."
The legal dispute dates back to February, when the DC Preservation League and others sued over redevelopment plans for the park.
The historic course, which sits two miles (3km) south of the White House, is one of three public courses run by the National Park Service (NPS) in the nation's capital.
The legal fight then escalated in October when the NPS began to cut down hundreds of trees without notifying Reyes until 15 hours before work was set to begin.
After the trees were cut, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to stop tree removal until at least 26 October and give her three business days' notice about making any other permanent changes.
Despite the work stoppage, Trump announced that the course would be closed for 15 months from 15 November to accommodate for the renovations. He also shared a rendering of the course redesign.

"The current Course is old, broken, dilapidated and of no further use or effect. It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous and disease-infested trees and, importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall," he said in a post on Truth Social.
Reyes has since separately opened an inquiry into whether justice department attorneys had "made misrepresentations to the court and otherwise violated ethical rules".

That included whether giving late notice to the court about the renovation plans had been "done in bad faith", and whether the attorneys failed to correct previously false statements or withheld information.
She said she would carry out the inquiry with a special master, an independent third party.
body_zh: 一名联邦法官暂时阻止美国政府关闭华盛顿特区一座历史悠久的高尔夫球场和公园。
美国地区法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 一直在监督对总统东波托马克高尔夫球场计划的长达数月的挑战，他表示东波托马克高尔夫球场将从 11 月 15 日起关闭，进行大规模翻修。
雷耶斯表示，唐纳德·特朗普总统不能关闭公园及其高尔夫球场，但他补充说，他的政府不需要积极管理。
特朗普是一名狂热的高尔夫球手，他表示，他计划升级这座拥有 106 年历史的球场，将打造“世界上最好、最壮观的高尔夫球场之一”。 BBC 已联系白宫请其置评。
他在 10 月份宣布当前的球场为“垃圾岛”，并宣布将在 15 个月内进行翻修，以打造一个“向公众开放，同时设计用于最高水平的高尔夫并能够举办世界级锦标赛”的空间——尽管诉讼仍在进行中。
雷耶斯在周六发布的一份长达 30 页的决定中表示，特朗普政府对拟议关闭课程的理由是借口，政府“为了在任意期限内完成任务”违反了至少两项联邦法律。
雷耶斯写道：“政府提议无限期关闭一座历史悠久的公园，华盛顿各种阶层的人每天都可以享受这个公园。”
她表示，关闭“与公众利用国家公园的利益背道而驰”，并补充说，政府尚未“合理地确定在进一步诉讼期间维持现状的临时限制令会对其造成任何损害”。
“垃圾岛”还是华盛顿的地标？高尔夫球场如何让特朗普陷入混乱的法律纠纷
反对关闭和翻修的倡导者和法律团体联盟表示，他们“感谢法院阻止政府非法关闭东波托马克公园并剥夺人们这一无价的美国历史和美妙的休闲空间”。
代表原告的联盟表示：“我们的法律阻止本届政府在没有公平和公开程序的情况下采取行动，今天的命令将阻止政府无视这些法律。”该联盟包括民主前进组织和民主捍卫者基金会。 “我们渴望继续在法庭上辩论此案。”
这场法律纠纷可以追溯到二月份，当时华盛顿特区保护联盟和其他组织就公园的重建计划提起诉讼。
这座历史悠久的球场位于白宫以南 2 英里（3 公里）处，是国家公园管理局 (NPS) 在美国首都运营的三个公共球场之一。
10 月份，法律斗争升级，NPS 开始砍伐数百棵树，但直到开工前 15 小时才通知雷耶斯。
树木被砍伐后，雷耶斯命令特朗普政府至少在 10 月 26 日之前停止砍伐树木，并提前三个工作日通知她做出任何其他永久性改变。
尽管停工，特朗普还是宣布球场将从 11 月 15 日起关闭 15 个月，以进行翻修。他还分享了课程重新设计的效果图。
他在Truth Social上发表的一篇文章中说：“目前的球场陈旧、破损、破旧，没有进一步的用途或影响。它的状况非常糟糕，有倒塌、危险和疾病肆虐的树木，更重要的是，还有倒塌和危险的海堤。”
此后，雷耶斯单独对司法部律师是否“向法庭作出虚假陈述以及其他违反道德规则的行为”展开调查。
其中包括向法院迟交有关翻修计划的通知是否“恶意”，以及律师是否未能纠正之前的虚假陈述或隐瞒信息。
她表示，她将由一位特别的大师（独立的第三方）进行调查。

title_en: Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
title_zh: 伊朗无人机袭击巴林美军基地
summary: It marks the second attack on the country in three days and comes as the US and Iran remain locked in a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz.
summary_zh: 这是三天内该国遭受的第二次袭击，发生之际美国和伊朗仍在霍尔木兹海峡陷入对峙。
body_en: Iran launched a drone attack against a US military base in Bahrain on Sunday, its second attempt to target the country in three days.
The country's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it targeted the US air defence radar facility at al-Riffa air base in Bahrain using six drones.
Bahrain's military said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed the Iranian air attacks "before they could achieve their objectives".
It comes after Iran fired drones at Bahrain on Friday, its first attack against Gulf countries since September.

The US and Iran are locked in a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz. About a fifth of the world's gas and oil supply usually flows through it but shipping has been restricted since the outbreak of war in February.

Iran insists that it should control the strait and has been attacking what it calls "unauthorised" traffic, while the US military is providing protection for tankers shuttling oil through the strait to keep exports flowing from Gulf Arab states.
As sirens sounded across Bahrain on Sunday the interior ministry called on citizens to head to their nearest safe location.

Bahrain's foreign ministry said: "The Kingdom of Bahrain condemns in the strongest terms the continued brutal Iranian attacks on its territory and holds Iran fully responsible for their consequences."

In a statement on the strikes shared by Iran's state broadcaster on Telegram, the IRGC said: "The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response."
Earlier this week, the IRGC claimed that it struck a US early warning radar system in Bahrain on Friday.
The US military has denied the claim, stating that the IRGC launched two one-way attack drones towards Bahrain and both were shot down by US forces. It added that there were no injuries or damage.
Earlier in the week the US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials told CBS, the BBC's US partner.
The officials described the strikes as limited and defensive, and said they were in response to the IRGC firing on a US aircraft.

Iranian state news agency Irna reported explosions on Qeshm on Monday. The IRGC did not comment but said its forces had shot down two US MQM-170 drones south of the island and a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated a naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Iranian negotiators had been discussing with mediators a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US meets seven conditions, reportedly including the lifting of the naval blockade and releasing frozen Iranian assets.

However this week Donald Trump said that the US was no longer interested in a deal to end the war with Iran and ordered Vice-President JD Vance, who had been involved in efforts to restart negotiations, to focus on domestic US politics.
Reported ship attacks near Strait of Hormuz hit record high
US strikes Iranian island ahead of midterm elections
body_zh: 伊朗周日对巴林的美国军事基地发动了无人机袭击，这是三天内第二次针对该国的袭击。
该国伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）表示，他们使用六架无人机瞄准了巴林阿尔里法空军基地的美国防空雷达设施。
巴林军方表示，其防空系统“在伊朗空袭实现目标之前”拦截并摧毁了他们。
此前，伊朗周五向巴林发射了无人机，这是自 9 月以来伊朗首次对海湾国家发动袭击。
美国和伊朗在霍尔木兹海峡陷入对峙。世界上大约五分之一的天然气和石油供应通常流经这里，但自二月份战争爆发以来，航运受到限制。
伊朗坚持认为应该控制该海峡，并一直在打击所谓的“未经授权”的交通，而美国军方正在为通过该海峡运送石油的油轮提供保护，以保证海湾阿拉伯国家的出口畅通。
周日，当巴林警报响起时，内政部呼吁公民前往最近的安全地点。
巴林外交部表示：“巴林王国以最强烈的措辞谴责伊朗对其领土的持续野蛮袭击，并要求伊朗对其后果承担全部责任。”
伊朗国家广播公司在 Telegram 上分享的有关此次袭击的声明中，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队表示：“霍尔木兹海峡已关闭，美国敌人的任何侵略都将遭到更严厉、更有力的回应。”
本周早些时候，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队声称周五袭击了位于巴林的美国预警雷达系统。
美国军方否认了这一说法，称伊斯兰革命卫队向巴林发射了两架单向攻击无人机，均被美军击落。它补充说，没有人员受伤或损坏。
美国官员告诉英国广播公司美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司，本周早些时候，美国对霍尔木兹海峡的伊朗格什姆岛进行了袭击。
官员们称这次袭击是有限的和防御性的，并表示这是对伊斯兰革命卫队向一架美国飞机开火的回应。
伊朗国家通讯社伊朗通讯社周一报道了格什姆岛发生爆炸事件。伊朗革命卫队没有发表评论，但表示其部队击落了该岛以南的两架美国 MQM-170 无人机和海峡以东的一架美国 MQ-9 无人机。
美国和伊朗于六月达成了结束战争并重新开放海峡的初步协议，但在伊朗恢复对航运的袭击以及美国恢复对伊朗港口的海上封锁后，该协议在几周内破裂。
伊朗谈判代表一直在与调解人讨论一项提议，如果美国满足七个条件，即在两天内重新开放霍尔木兹海峡，据报道包括解除海上封锁和释放冻结的伊朗资产。
然而本周唐纳德·特朗普表示，美国不再对结束与伊朗战争的协议感兴趣，并命令一直参与重启谈判努力的副总统万斯专注于美国国内政治。

title_en: South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating
title_zh: 韩国税务会计考试最高分承认作弊
summary: Han Won-seok, 34, confessed to using a hidden camera and AI to get a near-perfect mark on the significant test.
summary_zh: 34 岁的韩元石 (Han Won-seok) 承认，他使用隐藏摄像头和人工智能在这项重要测试中获得了近乎完美的分数。
body_en: A candidate who came first in South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam has admitted cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools.
Han Won-seok confessed in a video on the YouTube account of his lawyer, Lee Don-Ho, adding that he had confessed to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency and offered details on how he cheated.
The 34-year-old scored 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, getting just one of 160 questions wrong, which initially raised suspicions and sparked online speculation.
Standardised national tests play an outsized role in career trajectories for South Koreans, making their results - and efforts to unduly inflate those results - of great importance.
"I cheated in both the first and second rounds of the tax account exam by using electronic devices and generative AI," Han said in the video published on Sunday.
"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating."

When accusations he had cheated first began to surface, Han had denied any wrongdoing - but said he had changed his mind after thinking about the feelings of the candidate who had come second in the exam.
He went on to apologise to the other entrants who had passed the tests fairly.
"It seems that because of me, other successful candidates are being suspected," he suggested.
The Ministry of Employment and Labour and the Human Resources Development Service held an emergency meeting after Han admitted cheating.
The South Korean president's policy chief Ha Jun-kyung said new measures would be introduced to prevent cheating and warned "past crimes" would be "tracked down and apprehended to the very end".
Those found to have used AI to cheat in the tax accountancy exam will have their qualification revoked and will be banned from retaking the test for five years, the government said.
The scandal comes just days before the east Asian nation's annual college entrance exam, a crucial hurdle for students.
A series of cases involving exam cheating with AI glasses in South Korea has universities and schools scrambling to rein in the use of the technology.
Han said he had only cheated to try and earn money and get a job that would make his parents proud of him again.
Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency told Korean news agency Yonhap on Sunday that it was looking into the case.
"We received a written confession through the test taker's lawyer this morning regarding cheating on the tax accountant exam," it confirmed in a statement.
It added that the case had now been assigned to investigators.

Because of the significance of the national exams, instances of cheating are not uncommon in South Korea, and cases involving the use of AI have become more prominent as the technology becomes more sophisticated.
Last month, two college applicants were reported to have used AI glasses to try and cheat their entrance exams at two Seoul universities.
body_zh: 韩国注册税务会计考试第一名的考生承认使用微型相机、手机和人工智能工具作弊。
韩元石在其律师李敦浩的 YouTube 帐户上发布的一段视频中承认了自己的罪行，并补充说，他已向首尔警察厅认罪，并提供了有关他如何作弊的详细信息。
这位34岁的选手在第一轮比赛中获得了397.5分（满分400分），160道题中仅答错一题，这最初引起了人们的怀疑并引发了网上的猜测。
标准化的国家考试在韩国人的职业轨迹中发挥着巨大的作用，使得他们的结果 - 以及过度夸大这些结果的努力 - 非常重要。
“我在第一轮和第二轮税务账户考试中都通过使用电子设备和生成人工智能作弊，”韩在周日发布的视频中说。
“我用微型相机拍摄了测试问题，并将它们发送给人工智能，然后在我的智能手机上检查我的答案，以实施作弊。”
当他作弊的指控首次浮出水面时，韩否认有任何不当行为，但表示在考虑了考试中第二名考生的感受后，他改变了主意。
他接着向其他公平通过测试的参赛者道歉。
“似乎因为我，其他成功的候选人受到了怀疑，”他建议道。
在韩承认作弊后，就业和劳工部以及人力资源开发服务局召开了紧急会议。
韩国总统政策负责人河俊京表示，将采取新措施防止作弊，并警告称，“过去的犯罪行为”将被“追查到底并逮捕”。
政府表示，被发现在税务会计考试中使用人工智能作弊的人将被取消资格，并禁止在五年内重新参加考试。
这起丑闻发生在这个东亚国家一年一度的高考前几天，高考对学生来说是一个重要的障碍。
韩国发生了一系列涉及人工智能眼镜考试作弊的案件，促使大学和学校纷纷限制该技术的使用。
韩说，他作弊只是为了赚钱，找到一份能让父母再次为他感到骄傲的工作。
首尔警察厅周日告诉韩国联合通讯社，正在调查此案。
它在一份声明中证实：“今天早上，我们通过考生的律师收到了一份关于在税务会计师考试中作弊的书面供词。”
它补充说，此案现已分配给调查人员。
由于国家考试的重要性，作弊现象在韩国并不少见，而且随着技术的日益成熟，涉及人工智能的案件也变得更加突出。
上个月，据报道，两名大学申请者使用人工智能眼镜试图在首尔两所大学的入学考试中作弊。

title_en: 'Steering casualty' preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision, says NTSB
title_zh: 美国国家运输安全委员会表示，新奥尔良游轮相撞前发生了“转向伤亡”
summary: Preliminary findings by National Transportation Safety Board investigators suggest the tanker suffered a steering failure before colliding with the cruise ship on Friday.
summary_zh: 美国国家运输安全委员会调查人员的初步调查结果表明，这艘油轮在与卡车相撞之前发生了转向故障。
body_en: The tanker that struck a cruise ship docked in New Orleans on Friday had a "steering casualty", officials said, citing preliminary findings into the collision.
It remains unclear what caused the steering failure on the Atlantic Asphalt cargo vessel, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said in a media briefing on Sunday.
The collision left 32 people from the stricken American Heritage riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one was unaccounted for.
The NTSB said there are many different things that could be classified as a steering casualty, and they are "looking at all of them".
New Orleans port files $1m lawsuit over 'miracle on the Mississippi' tanker collision
The tanker was upbound on the Mississippi River as it moved toward the east bank of the river just before the collision, said the NTSB, based on findings from the vessel's voyage data recorder.
Minutes before the crash, investigators said audio consistent with the ship's warning system was broadcast, along with commands to deploy the vessel's anchors and emergency ship handling orders.

"We are aware that there was an issue with the steering on board and causing the rudder to remain at a starboard position, causing the heading of the vessel to veer towards the east bank," investigator-in-charge Bart Barnum said during the news conference.
The exact issue with the steering has yet to be determined, he added.
A preliminary report from the NTSB is expected in 30 days.

Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll said after the incident.
There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority.
Passengers began getting off the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping onto its side.
Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort.
The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway.

body_zh: 官员们援引碰撞的初步调查结果称，周五撞上停靠在新奥尔良的一艘游轮的油轮造成了“舵轮伤亡”。
美国国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）在周日的媒体吹风会上表示，目前尚不清楚大西洋沥青货船转向失灵的原因。
这次碰撞导致受损的 American Heritage 河船上的 32 人被送往医院，伤势不重，但没有人下落不明。
美国国家运输安全委员会表示，有很多不同的情况可以被归类为转向事故，他们正在“研究所有这些情况”。
新奥尔良港口因“密西西比河奇迹”油轮相撞事件提起 100 万美元诉讼
美国国家运输安全委员会根据该船航行数据记录仪的调查结果表示，在碰撞发生前，这艘油轮正在密西西比河上行，并向河东岸移动。
事故发生前几分钟，调查人员表示，广播了与船舶警报系统一致的音频，以及部署船舶锚的命令和紧急船舶处理命令。
调查负责人巴特·巴纳姆在新闻发布会上表示：“我们意识到船上的转向系统存在问题，导致舵保持在右舷位置，导致船只转向东岸。”
他补充说，转向系统的具体问题尚未确定。
NTSB 预计将在 30 天内发布初步报告。
新奥尔良港负责人梅兰妮·蒙特罗尔 (Melanie Montroll) 在新闻发布会上表示，有关碰撞的电话于周五 13:30（格林尼治标准时间 18:30）左右开始出现，当时人们开始试图帮助乘客在船进水时逃生。
据港务局称，事故发生时，美国遗产号上除船员外，还有大约 129 名乘客。
莫雷诺说，这艘由美国邮轮公司运营的明轮船开始倾斜，然后侧翻，乘客们开始下船。
拖船操作员、警察和其他救援人员赶来提供帮助，同时官员在救援过程中关闭了密西西比河的交通。
美国遗产号已经结束了为期八天的航行，沿途停靠路易斯安那州和密西西比州的目的地。

title_en: England stun Spain to end La Roja’s 43-game unbeaten run
title_zh: 英格兰队击败西班牙队终结了西班牙队43场不败的纪录
summary: Spain suffer first defeat since March 2024 after losing 3-2 to England in Madrid despite grandstand finish.
summary_zh: 尽管看台结束，西班牙在马德里以 3-2 输给英格兰，但遭遇了自 2024 年 3 月以来的首场失利。
body_en: England stun Spain to end La Roja’s 43-game unbeaten run | Football News | Al Jazeera
Share World Champions Spain beaten 3-2 by 10-man England in Madrid on social media
England held on with 10 men to record a stunning win over Spain in Madrid in one of the great UEFA Nations League games.

The visitors had seen their hosts parade their World Cup trophy on the pitch before the game, but raced into a 3-0 lead inside an hour, before being reduced to 10 men on 65 minutes and having to cling on in a dramatic finale to pip Spain to top spot in Group A3 on goal difference.

It was a record 10th straight away win for the Three Lions, and it inflicted the first defeat on La Roja since they went down 1-0 in a friendly against Colombia in London in March 2024. The 43-game run saw them crowned European and World Champions along the way.
England produced a stunning start and might have been ahead inside the opening minutes, but Unai Simon made a brilliant reaction save to claw away Jude Bellingham’s close-range effort.

The visitors were irresistible in the first half, pressing high and denying the hosts time and space to find their rhythm, and Spain were unable to register a shot on target in the opening 45 minutes.

England led 1-0 at the break after Harry Kane latched onto Elliot Anderson’s pass in behind and drew a foul from Pau Cubarsi in the box. Following a brief VAR review into Anderson’s challenge on Marc Cucurella in the build-up, Kane stepped up to convert the penalty.
He fired to the right of Unai Simon to register his 93rd Three Lions goal on his 127th appearance in the final seconds of the half.
The visitors doubled their lead eight minutes after the turnaround as Declan Rice’s curling corner was met by a powerful downward header from the unmarked Ezri Konsa, his Arsenal teammate.

The hosts were in disarray four minutes later, when some slick counterattacking saw Bellingham slot through into space on the right of the box for the on-rushing Ben White to drill a low shot past Simon at his near post.

The game changed 25 minutes from time when Jarell Quansah was dispossessed in his own half, and Anderson was shown a straight red card for denying a goalscoring opportunity by putting his arm on Lamine Yamal as he raced into the box.
After VAR confirmed the decision, Mikel Oyarzabal sent James Trafford – recalled in place of Jordan Pickford in goal – the wrong way to give the hosts hope.
They piled on the pressure and reduced the arrears further on the break on 75 minutes, when Yamal’s first-time cross from the right was swept in off the post by substitute Nico Williams.

La Roja laid siege to the England goal in the closing stages as they sought a goal to extend their unbeaten run and claim top spot in Group A3. But Trafford produced a stunning double save in stoppage time, diving to his right to parry a shot from Fermin Lopez, then somehow bouncing up to turn the follow-up from Aymeric Laporte around the upright.
England held on to secure first place in the group on goal difference after both sides finished on 15 points.

Both sides will find out their Nations League quarterfinal opponents next March when the draw takes place on Friday. England is set to face one of the three A-Group runners-up, other than Spain, while La Roja will face one of the other three group winners.
body_zh: 英格兰队击败西班牙队终结了西班牙队43场不败的纪录足球新闻|半岛电视台
在社交媒体上分享 世界冠军西班牙队在马德里被十人应战的英格兰队以 3-2 击败
英格兰队在马德里以 10 人的战绩击败了西班牙队，这是一场伟大的欧洲国家联赛。
赛前，客队在球场上目睹了东道主在球场上展示世界杯奖杯，但他们在一小时内就以 3-0 领先，但在 65 分钟内人数减少到 10 人，不得不在戏剧性的决赛中以净胜球优势击败西班牙队，夺得 A3 组头名。
这是三狮军团创纪录的客场第十连胜，也是自 2024 年 3 月在伦敦对阵哥伦比亚的友谊赛中以 1-0 落败后，西班牙队首次遭遇失利。在 43 场比赛中，他们一路加冕欧洲冠军和世界冠军。
英格兰队取得了令人惊叹的开局，在开场几分钟内就可能领​​先，但乌奈·西蒙做出了精彩的反应，扑救了裘德·贝林厄姆的近距离射门。
客队在上半场势不可挡，高位逼抢，剥夺了主队找到节奏的时间和空间，西班牙队在开场45分钟内未能射正。
中场休息时，哈里·凯恩接到埃利奥特·安德森的传球，并在禁区内制造了保罗·库巴斯的犯规，英格兰队以1-0领先。在对安德森在进攻中对马克·库库雷拉的挑战进行了简短的VAR审查后，凯恩挺身而出将点球罚进。
他在半场最后几秒向乌奈·西蒙右侧射门，这是他第 127 次出场，这是他在三狮军团的第 93 个进球。
比赛结束八分钟后，客队将领先优势扩大一倍，德克兰·赖斯开出弧线角球，无人盯防的阿森纳队友埃兹里·孔萨强力头球攻门，客队将领先优势扩大一倍。
四分钟后，主队陷入混乱，贝林厄姆巧妙的反击进入禁区右侧的空间，冲上来的本怀特在近门柱处低射越过西蒙。
比赛进行到25分钟后，比赛发生了变化，贾雷尔·夸萨在本方半场被剥夺了球权，安德森在冲进禁区时用手臂抵住拉明·亚马尔，从而拒绝了进球机会，直接被出示红牌。
在VAR确认了这一决定后，米克尔·奥亚扎瓦尔（Mikel Oyarzabal）向詹姆斯·特拉福德（James Trafford）（被召回代替乔丹·皮克福德（Jordan Pickford）担任门将）错误的方式给了主队希望。
第75分钟，亚马尔第一次从右路传中，替补出场的尼科·威廉姆斯将球从门柱上扫过，他们加大了压力，进一步减少了落后。
拉罗亚队在最后阶段围攻了英格兰队的球门，他们力求进球以延续不败纪录，并在A3组中夺得头名。但特拉福德在补时阶段做出了令人惊叹的两次扑救，他向右扑出费明·洛佩兹的射门，然后又以某种方式弹起，将艾默里克·拉波尔特的跟进球绕过了直立的球门。
英格兰队在双方同积15分后，凭借净胜球优势锁定小组第一。
双方将于明年三月周五抽签时选出各自的国联四分之一决赛对手。英格兰队将对阵西班牙以外的三支A组亚军之一，而拉罗亚队将对阵另外三支小组冠军之一。

title_en: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
title_zh: Megaspeed 称，与 Nvidia 前老板有联系的疑似中国间谍将于 2025 年离职
summary: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.
summary_zh: 英伟达丑闻引发了人们的疑问：尽管美国有限制，先进的人工智能芯片是否最终会进入中国。
body_en: By Dearbail Jordan , Business reporter and Lily Jamali , North America Technology correspondent , Reporting from Palo Alto, CA
Alice Huang, a suspected China spy who has been linked to Nvidia's former boss Jensen Huang, left her executive role at Megaspeed in August last year, the company says.
Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees.

Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.
Megaspeed said it was aware of reports "containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence".
It added that it "conducts legitimate and lawful business" and has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation".

Also on Sunday, US Congressman John Moolenaar said that Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the Select Committee on China, which he chairs, as well as the House Foreign Affairs and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.
The committee heads had threatened to issue subpoenas to Huang if he did not comply with their requests to testify.
Moolenaar told CBS, BBC's US partner, that none were ultimately issued. Huang's testimony is expected to take place behind close doors, with the dates still being finalised.

"That's going to be a very important meeting to understand to what degree privileged information was accessed, and to what degree this potential alleged Chinese spy influenced Nvidia's philosophy and may have had an influence on some of our policies with respect to AI and export controls," the congressman told the Face The Nation programme.
Separately, a group of tech leaders, including Space X's Elon Musk, have been trying to rally support to have Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO.
A representative for Huang declined to comment on a report in the Financial Times Sunday suggesting that he was discussing a comeback to the firm he co-founded.
On Friday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed fellow Trump cabinet colleague Howard Lutnick's commerce department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-end chips.
Bessent told CNBC that several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months... but Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process".
The so-called entity list restricts US trade with overseas firms and individuals.
Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over his department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.
Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Jensen Huang.
Megaspeed is suspected of giving backdoor access to Nvidia chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
body_zh: 作者：商业记者 Dearbail Jordan 和北美科技记者 Lily Jamali，加利福尼亚州帕洛阿尔托报道
该公司表示，与英伟达前老板黄仁勋有联系的涉嫌中国间谍的爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 于去年 8 月辞去 Megaspeed 的高管职务。
黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 辞去了人工智能芯片制造巨头英伟达 (Nvidia) 首席执行官的职务，因为他涉嫌与 Alice Huang 及其一名员工有染。
Megaspeed 是 Nvidia 芯片在东南亚的最大买家，Nvidia 的丑闻引发了人们的质疑，即尽管美国实施出口限制，高端 AI 芯片最终可能会销往中国。
这家总部位于新加坡的公司周日表示，已对其业务展开内部调查。
Megaspeed 表示，它知道有报道“包含有关我们业务、供应链和全球运营的断言，但这些断言没有可验证的证据支持”。
它补充说，它“开展合法合法的业务”，并“聘请了外部法律顾问来进行彻底的内部调查”。
同样在周日，美国国会议员约翰·莫勒纳尔表示，黄仁勋已同意在他担任主席的中国问题特别委员会以及众议院外交事务和众议院情报常设特别委员会面前作证。
委员会负责人威胁说，如果黄不遵守他们的作证要求，就会向他发出传票。
穆勒纳尔告诉 BBC 美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司，最终没有发布任何内容。黄的作证预计将闭门进行，日期仍在敲定中。
这位国会议员告诉 Face The Nation 节目：“这将是一次非常重要的会议，旨在了解特权信息被获取的程度，以及这名潜在的被指控的中国间谍在多大程度上影响了英伟达的理念，并可能对我们在人工智能和出口管制方面的一些政策产生了影响。”
另外，包括 Space X 的埃隆·马斯克在内的一批科技领袖一直在努力争取支持，让黄仁勋重新担任 Nvidia 首席执行官。
黄的代表拒绝对周日英国《金融时报》的一篇报道发表评论，该报道暗示黄正在讨论重返他共同创立的公司。
周五，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特指责特朗普内阁同事霍华德·卢特尼克的商务部未能妥善监管高端芯片的出口。
Bessent 告诉 CNBC，数家机构“几个月来一直赞成将 Megaspeed 列入实体名单……但商务部有笔……你必须询问他们的内部流程”。
所谓的实体清单限制美国与海外公司和个人的贸易。
卢特尼克下个月被要求在参议院银行委员会就其部门在允许英伟达出口其先进芯片方面所扮演的角色作证。
其他国会委员会已要求卢特尼克及其部门保留与 Nvidia 和黄仁勋有关的所有记录。
Megaspeed 涉嫌通过其位于马来西亚、印度尼西亚和泰国的数据中心向中国公司提供对 Nvidia 芯片的后门访问。

title_en: Goodbye, overtourism? Sustainable travel gains ground
title_zh: 再见，过度旅游？可持续旅游取得进展
summary: As tourism booms across Latin America, alternative forms of travel are gaining ground. Making your holiday more sustainable means rethinking who calls the shots, who invests and who benefits.
summary_zh: 随着拉丁美洲旅游业的蓬勃发展，另类旅行方式正在普及。让您的假期更加可持续意味着重新考虑谁打电话
body_en: Latin America is currently one of the world's most dynamic tourism regions. According to UN Tourism, the United Nations agency responsible for promoting responsible tourism, international arrivals in South America grew by 7% last year, while Central America saw a 5% increase, both above the global average.

But the boom comes at a price: overtourism . In some destinations, the sheer number of visitors is creating environmental and social problems , fueling tensions and raising questions about who really benefits from the business.

One famous example is Machu Picchu, the Inca citadel in Peru, which lures up to 5,600 visitors a day. In 2025, Peru's official watchdog warned that more tickets were being sold than permitted, potentially putting the site at risk of being added to UNESCO's List of World Heritage in Danger . The UNESCO World Heritage Committee has already expressed its concern.

In a bid to protect the Galapagos Islands and its bountiful ecosystems that inspired Charles Darwin, Ecuador doubled the entrance fee for foreign visitors to $200 in 2024. Even so, pressure is mounting to construct new hotels and tourist apartments. And in Mexico City, the influx of tourists and digital nomads into neighborhoods such as Roma and Condesa has fueled protests over rising rents.

What can be done to make tourism more inclusive and sustainable? That's one of the industry's biggest questions. At ITB Americas, an international travel trade fair in Guadalajara, Mexico, DW spoke with three experts.
Sustainable travel moving from niche to mainstream

Richard Bazan is a regional manager for the Americas at Planeterra, a nonprofit organization that promotes and supports community-based tourism. He said several trends are emerging: group sizes are shrinking and travelers are seeking more intimate experiences.
"Where groups of 20 used to travel together, now it's four or five," he told DW.

So-called "nature-positive" tourism is also gaining traction, with travel programs that help fund, for example, reforestation projects. Bazan said even all-inclusive resorts are realizing that they can no longer shut themselves off from their surroundings. Instead, they need to offer authentic experiences that connect visitors with the destination.
"Community-based tourism is no longer a niche," he said.

Pressure for change is also coming from travelers themselves. According to Booking.com's 2025 annual survey, which polled 32,000 people in 34 countries, 93% said they wanted to make more sustainable travel choices. For the first time, more than half (53%) were aware of tourism's impact on local communities, not just the environment.

Sarah Payne, director of the Reset Tourism Fund at the UnTours Foundation, pointed to the underlying problem. In the traditional tourism business model, most of the money generated never reaches local communities, the people who actually live with the influx of visitors.

"Access to financing is key, yet extremely difficult for communities," she explained. The financial products on the market tend to be expensive and inflexible, as tourism is considered a high-risk sector. Her foundation's fund offers low-interest loans with flexible repayment terms. Its guiding principle is that communities generally know what's best for their own land.

Sebastian Munoz, co-founder of Rutopia, a platform specializing in ecotourism and community-based tourism, has brought his experience from the nonprofit sector into social enterprise. His believes tours must be designed in partnership with communities so they feel a sense of ownership, rather than seeing them as something imposed from outside.

Bazan, meanwhile, thinks community-based tourism should not be approached as a humanitarian project, but through a market-driven lens: understanding what visitors are looking for and then planning hand-in-hand with the local community. In other words, building bridges between these two distinct worlds.
"It's not sustainable to create a product if no one comes to experience it," he said.

The big question is how to grow without sacrificing sustainability. For Bazan, that decision doesn't belong to the tourism industry. Communities themselves must decide how they want to grow, and outside players should not pressure them. Their role, he said, is to amplify local voices, not to bring solutions or investments. "We have to learn to listen," he said.

The impact of community-based tourism is difficult to measure, Munoz acknowledged, because it has social impacts that go beyond the numbers. He cited the example of the Indigenous Mixtec community in Mexico that receives tourists interested in learning the local language. Suddenly, children who today speak only Spanish began joining the classes and asking their grandparents to teach them the language, too.
body_zh: 拉丁美洲目前是世界上最具活力的旅游地区之一。据负责促进负责任旅游的联合国机构联合国旅游局称，去年南美洲的国际游客增长了 7%，而中美洲则增长了 5%，均高于全球平均水平。
但繁荣是有代价的：过度旅游。在一些目的地，游客数量之多正在造成环境和社会问题，加剧紧张局势，并引发人们对谁真正从这项业务中受益的疑问。
一个著名的例子是秘鲁的印加城堡马丘比丘，每天吸引多达 5,600 名游客。 2025 年，秘鲁官方监管机构警告称，出售的门票数量超出允​​许范围，这可能会使该遗址面临被列入联合国教科文组织濒危世界遗产名录的风险。联合国教科文组织世界遗产委员会已经表达了担忧。
为了保护加拉帕戈斯群岛及其丰富的生态系统（启发了查尔斯·达尔文），厄瓜多尔在 2024 年将外国游客的入场费提高了一倍，达到 200 美元。即便如此，建造新酒店和旅游公寓的压力越来越大。在墨西哥城，游客和数字游民涌入罗马和康德萨等社区，引发了针对租金上涨的抗议活动。
如何使旅游业更具包容性和可持续性？这是该行业最大的问题之一。在墨西哥瓜达拉哈拉举行的国际旅游贸易展览会 ITB Americas 上，德国之声采访了三位专家。
可持续旅游从小众走向主流
Richard Bazan 是 Planeterra 的美洲区域经理，Planeterra 是一家促进和支持社区旅游业的非营利组织。他说，一些趋势正在出现：团体规模正在缩小，旅行者正在寻求更亲密的体验。
他告诉德国之声：“以前是20人一起旅行，现在是四五个人一起旅行。”
所谓的“积极自然”旅游业也越来越受欢迎，其旅游项目有助于资助重新造林项目等。巴赞说，即使是全包式度假村也意识到他们不能再将自己与周围环境隔绝。相反，他们需要提供真实的体验，将游客与目的地联系起来。
“以社区为基础的旅游不再是一个利基市场，”他说。
改变的压力也来自旅行者本身。 Booking.com 的 2025 年年度调查对 34 个国家的 32,000 人进行了调查，结果显示，93% 的人表示希望做出更可持续的旅行选择。超过一半（53%）的人第一次意识到旅游业对当地社区的影响，而不仅仅是环境。
UnTours 基金会重置旅游基金主任莎拉·佩恩指出了根本问题。在传统的旅游商业模式中，产生的大部分资金从未到达当地社区，而这些社区实际上是与游客涌入一起生活的人们。
“获得融资是关键，但对社区来说却极其困难，”她解释道。由于旅游业被认为是高风险行业，市场上的金融产品往往价格昂贵且缺乏灵活性。她的基金会的基金提供低息贷款和灵活的还款条件。其指导原则是社区普遍知道什么对自己的土地最有利。
专门从事生态旅游和社区旅游的平台 Rutopia 的联合创始人塞巴斯蒂安·穆尼奥斯 (Sebastian Munoz) 将他在非营利部门的经验带入了社会企业。他认为旅游必须与社区合作设计，让他们有一种主人翁感，而不是将其视为外部强加的东西。
拯救拉达克：当地人引领可持续旅游业发展
要观看此视频，请启用 JavaScript，并考虑升级到支持 HTML5 视频的网络浏览器
与此同时，巴赞认为，基于社区的旅游业不应被视为一项人道主义项目，而应通过市场驱动的视角来对待：了解游客的需求，然后与当地社区携手规划。换句话说，在这两个不同的世界之间架起桥梁。
“如果没有人来体验它，那么创造一种产品是不可持续的，”他说。
最大的问题是如何在不牺牲可持续性的情况下实现增长。对于巴赞来说，这个决定不属于旅游业。社区自己必须决定如何发展，外部参与者不应向他们施加压力。他说，他们的作用是放大当地的声音，而不是带来解决方案或投资。 “我们必须学会倾听，”他说。
穆尼奥斯承认，基于社区的旅游业的影响很难衡量，因为它的社会影响超出了数字。他引用了墨西哥米斯特克原住民社区的例子，该社区接待有兴趣学习当地语言的游客。突然间，现在只会说西班牙语的孩子们开始加入课堂，并要求他们的祖父母也教他们这门语言。

title_en: Africa CDC says Ebola outbreak in DR Congo ‘still not under control’
title_zh: 非洲疾病预防控制中心表示刚果民主共和国的埃博拉疫情“仍未得到控制”
summary: 'If we don't stop this outbreak now, it would be the worst Ebola outbreak,' Africa ​CDC director says.
summary_zh: 非洲疾病预防控制中心主任表示，如果我们现在不阻止这次疫情爆发，这将是最严重的埃博拉疫情。
body_en: Share Africa CDC says Ebola outbreak in DR Congo ‘still not under control’ on social media
Africa’s top public health agency says the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is still not under control six months after it was declared.

“If we don’t stop this outbreak now, it would be the worst Ebola outbreak that the world will have,” Jean Kaseya, director-general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), told Reuters news agency on Sunday.

Since the outbreak was announced on May 15, more than 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths have been recorded, according to government data.
Kaseya said that more than “80 percent of ‌new cases emerge outside contact lists and over 65 percent of deaths” have occurred in the community outside health centres.
Cases have now been reported in East, Central and West Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.
“We are all in agreement today to say that this outbreak is still serious, and is ⁠still not under control,” Kaseya said.
The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which can trigger haemorrhagic fever.
It is the second-largest and second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, behind only the 2014-2016 West African outbreak. That epidemic infected more than 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000.
Eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces have been affected in the ongoing outbreak, and many deaths have occurred outside treatment centres.
Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have led to a more rapid spread of the virus than in previous outbreaks.
Kaseya said coordination between DRC and donors remained a problem, calling it “a collective failure”.
Only $1.3bn of the $2.9bn pledged by donors to fight Ebola has been released, according to Kaseya.

“We are not pointing fingers,” he said, adding that Africa CDC was working closely with Kinshasa to ensure money isn’t wasted ‌through ‌duplication and that the DRC was working to digitise the payroll to health workers who “hadn’t been paid for months”.
Containment has been especially difficult because no vaccine or treatment has been developed specifically for the Bundibugyo strain, which kills about half of the people it infects.
Earlier this month, the World Health Organization (WHO) approved clinical trials of two new Ebola vaccines and said it expected results in early 2027.

“Transmission is slowing in several early epicentres, and clinical trials, including the Tumaini trial and new vaccine candidates, are advancing rapidly”, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus wrote in a post on X.
body_zh: 分享 非洲 疾病预防控制中心在社交媒体上表示刚果民主共和国的埃博拉疫情“仍未得到控制”
非洲最高公共卫生机构表示，刚果民主共和国（DRC）的埃博拉疫情在宣布六个月后仍未得到控制。
非洲疾病控制和预防中心（非洲疾病预防控制中心）总干事让·卡塞亚周日对路透社表示：“如果我们现在不阻止疫情爆发，这将是世界上最严重的埃博拉疫情。”
3 项清单 3 项中的 1 项炭疽爆发导致刚果民主共和国维龙加国家公园的河马死亡
list 2 of 3 卫生当局正在尼日利亚东北部调查两例埃博拉疑似病例
刚果民主共和国埃博拉死亡人数已超过 5,000 人，共 3 人
根据政府数据，自 5 月 15 日宣布疫情爆发以来，已有超过 11,200 例病例和 5,500 人死亡。
卡塞亚说，“超过 80% 的新病例出现在接触名单之外，超过 65% 的死亡”发生在卫生中心以外的社区。
目前，东非、中非和西非均报告了病例，是迄今为止该大陆埃博拉疫情中地理分布最广的一次。
卡塞亚说：“我们今天一致认为，这次疫情仍然很严重，并且仍未得到控制。”
此次疫情是由罕见的埃博拉病毒本迪布焦株引起的，该株可引发出血热。
这是有记录以来第二大、第二致命的埃博拉疫情，仅次于 2014-2016 年西非疫情。那次流行病感染了 28,600 多人，并导致 11,000 多人死亡。
刚果民主共和国 26 个省中有 8 个省受到当前疫情的影响，许多人死亡发生在治疗中心外。
检测延迟、冲突和卫生服务紧张导致病毒传播速度比之前的疫情更快。
卡塞亚表示，刚果民主共和国与捐助者之间的协调仍然是一个问题，称其为“集体失败”。
卡塞亚表示，捐助者承诺抗击埃博拉病毒的 29 亿美元中，只有 13 亿美元已经到位。
他说：“我们不是在指责。”他补充说，非洲疾病预防控制中心正在与金沙萨密切合作，以确保资金不会因重复而浪费，刚果民主共和国正在努力将“几个月没有领到工资”的卫生工作者的工资单数字化。
遏制工作尤其困难，因为目前还没有专门针对本迪布焦毒株开发出疫苗或治疗方法，该毒株导致大约一半的感染者死亡。
本月早些时候，世界卫生组织 (WHO) 批准了两种新型埃博拉疫苗的临床试验，并表示预计将于 2027 年初获得结果。
世卫组织总干事谭德塞在 X 上发表的一篇文章中写道：“几个早期疫情中心的传播正在放缓，包括图迈尼试验和新候选疫苗在内的临床试验正在迅速推进。”

title_en: Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink restrictions and be on 'right side of history'
title_zh: 泽伦斯基敦促美国和马斯克取消星链限制并站在“历史正确的一边”
summary: The Ukrainian president says the slowed-down internet is making it difficult to stop Russian attacks.
summary_zh: 乌克兰总统表示，速度缓慢的互联网使得阻止俄罗斯的攻击变得困难。
body_en: A crucial US satellite internet service is still operating too slowly and affecting Ukraine's ability to stop Russian attacks, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
"We are counting on these restrictions being lifted. The protection of lives and Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of winter directly depends on this," he said.
The issue over the speed of the Starshield system - a military-grade Starlink service owned by Elon Musk and provided to Ukraine by the US government - has been rumbling on for weeks.

Zelensky said he had asked officials "to work as closely as possible" with the US government and Musk's company. "It is important to be on the right side of history," he said. The BBC has asked the White House and Starlink for comment.
US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
Ukraine uses the normal Starlink service for communications on the battlefield, while Starshield is used for the interception of missiles and drones in Ukraine airspace.
The issue of speed restrictions was first identified in October. It led to conflicting accounts by both Elon Musk and US President Donald Trump.
Musk said the US government was responsible as Starshield was controlled by them, but Trump denied being responsible and said he had told the billionaire owner to "put it back".
It appeared to be returning to normal after a week, following which Ukraine said the restrictions were still being implemented.
The connection issues coincided with a tense diplomatic stand-off between Zelensky and Trump over Ukrainian strikes on oil infrastructure within Russia.
Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow's war effort, had pushed global prices higher.

On Sunday Zelensky said Ukraine was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones targeting electricity substations because "restrictions on the operating speed of Starshield terminals along the front line and in the temporarily occupied territories are still there".

"Our interceptor drones lose connection with their operators at a speed of 161km/h (100mph) and simply cannot catch up with Russian jet-powered 'shaheds'," he posted, referring to the drones that follow an Iranian design.
On Friday Zelensky said speed limits of around 100mph had been enforced on the network since Monday, but only in Russian-occupied areas and not the whole of Ukraine.

"It already has political implications. If you impose restrictions there, you are already partially recognising the temporary occupied territories as not ours," the New York Times reported him as saying.
Ukraine has also been beset by a shortage of US-made Patriot interceptors used to defend against Russian missiles - a situation that Russia has exploited to intensify strikes on Ukrainian targets.
Overnight and into Sunday morning Russia hit energy infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia and the Sumy, Odesa, Zhytomyr, and Kirovohrad regions, Ukraine said.
It also struck railway infrastructure in the Dnipro, Kharkiv, and Zaporizhzhia regions.
Scores of people are said to have been hurt in those attacks, as well as two in the Donetsk and Kyiv regions.
Two people were killed in an attack on an infrastructure facility in Chernihiv Region's Mena, governor Vyacheslav Chaus said.

“我们指望这些限制能够被取消。冬季到来之前对生命和乌克兰能源基础设施的保护直接取决于这一点，”他说。
关于“星盾”系统（由埃隆·马斯克拥有、由美国政府向乌克兰提供的军用级星链服务）的速度问题已经持续了数周。
泽伦斯基表示，他已要求官员与美国政府和马斯克的公司“尽可能密切合作”。 “站在历史正确的一边很重要，”他说。 BBC 已要求白宫和 Starlink 发表评论。
泽伦斯基表示，美国已提议乌克兰放弃顿巴斯以加入北约
乌克兰使用普通的星链服务进行战场通信，而星盾则用于拦截乌克兰领空的导弹和无人机。
限速问题于 10 月份首次被发现。这导致埃隆·马斯克和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的说法相互矛盾。
马斯克表示，美国政府应对星盾负责，因为星盾是由他们控制的，但特朗普否认对此负责，并表示他已告诉这位亿万富翁老板“把它放回去”。
一周后情况似乎恢复正常，随后乌克兰表示仍在实施限制。
这些连接问题恰逢泽伦斯基和特朗普之间因乌克兰袭击俄罗斯境内石油基础设施而陷入紧张的外交对峙。
特朗普表示，对俄罗斯炼油厂的袭击推高了全球油价，基辅称这对于阻止莫斯科战争的主要收入来源至关重要。
泽伦斯基周日表示，乌克兰正在努力拦截针对变电站的俄罗斯喷气式无人机，因为“前线和临时占领领土上的星盾终端运行速度仍然受到限制”。
“我们的拦截无人机以 161 公里/小时（100 英里/小时）的速度与操作员失去联系，根本无法追上俄罗斯喷气动力‘沙赫德’，”他指的是遵循伊朗设计的无人机。
泽连斯基周五表示，自周一以来，该网络已实施约 100 英里/小时的限速，但仅限于俄罗斯占领地区，而不是整个乌克兰。
据《纽约时报》报道，他说：“这已经产生了政治影响。如果你在那里施加限制，你就已经部分承认临时占领的领土不属于我们。”
乌克兰还受到用于防御俄罗斯导弹的美制爱国者拦截机短缺的困扰，俄罗斯利用这种情况加强了对乌克兰目标的打击。
乌克兰称，从一夜之间到周日早上，俄罗斯袭击了扎波罗热、苏梅、敖德萨、日托米尔和基洛沃拉德地区的能源基础设施。
它还袭击了第聂伯罗、哈尔科夫和扎波罗热地区的铁路基础设施。
据称，数十人在这些袭击中受伤，顿涅茨克和基辅地区也有两人受伤。
切尔尼戈夫州梅纳州州长维亚切斯拉夫·乔斯 (Vyacheslav Chaus) 表示，切尔尼戈夫州梅纳州一处基础设施遭到袭击，造成两人死亡。
